doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Scale pay then, and Kind of Blue
summary: Comparing Jimmy Cobb's pay on Kind of Blue, they estimate scale in the late 1950s and 1960s.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And then on the other hand there’s anecdotes like Jimmy Cobb the drummer who played on “Kind of Blue?” He made like less than a hundred bucks for that thing.

Well scale like I say is much different now. But again not that many people use studio players anymore. Like I say in Nashville the country records, it’s still mostly studio guys. I know they still put together jazz groups to play in the studio. But “Kind of Blue,” what year was that? Early 60s?
Gosh I doubt if scale then was even 54 bucks.
Yeah I think it was in the 40s or 50s for a three hour session or something.
I think when I started it was like 75 bucks for a three hour session and then I went to double scale.
